senses.sense_definition: A priest who listens to personal confessions of sins and grants absolution.

examples.text: He spoke softly to his <w>confessor</w> through the screen in the darkened church.
The king trusted his personal <w>confessor</w> with his deepest spiritual concerns.

senses.sense_definition: A person who acts as a trusted, sympathetic listener to someone's private troubles or secrets.

examples.text: Over the years, she had become a trusted friend and <w>confessor</w> to everyone in the office.
He did not need advice, only a patient <w>confessor</w> who would hear his story without judgment.

senses.sense_definition: A person who admits to or confesses having done something wrong.

examples.text: The police questioned the voluntary <w>confessor</w> to verify details of the crime.
Investigators were skeptical of each self-proclaimed <w>confessor</w> who came forward.

senses.sense_definition: In Christianity, a person who maintains their faith under severe persecution without suffering martyrdom.

examples.text: King Edward was honored as a saint and a <w>confessor</w> rather than a martyr.
Early church communities showed immense reverence to every surviving <w>confessor</w>.
